issue.title: Secret-typed gate inputs leak: raw sidecar copies, crackable journal digest, clipboard copy-out, no mobile refusal
issue.description:
Discovered during sudo-agent-password research consolidation (research bundle
202609/agent_sudo_requests). The generic `secret: true` gate-input path promises
redaction but leaks the raw secret value, or a crackable derivative, at several
file-level points. All findings verified by direct code reading at commit
8ed00c4ed6; no live reproduction with a real secret was run.

1. Detached gate answers write raw secrets to disk. `_submit_detached_answer`
   copies `option_inputs` unredacted into the proc operation-request payload
   (src/sase/notification_gates/cli_answer.py:288-289) which
   `submit_proc_request` persists to
   `~/.sase/procs/runtime/<proc>/operation-request.json` (mode 0600, retained
   until proc-history pruning), and echoes them raw in its return payload
   (cli_answer.py:321), which flows into operation-result.json and the proc's
   `--json` output log. Shell-backed gates default to detached
   (cli_answer.py:253-265), and ACE's own answer proc adds further sidecar
   copies (src/sase/ace/tui/actions/agents/_notification_gate_execution.py).
2. The journal digest is an offline-cracking oracle for human passwords:
   `value_digest` is unsalted sha256(canonical_json(value))
   (src/sase/notification_gates/journal.py:74-76), recorded per option for
   retry matching. For a low-entropy secret in a small known JSON shape this is
   dictionary-crackable, so redacting the plaintext does not help.
3. The secret widget masks rendering only: `SecretVimTextArea`'s docstring
   documents that vim registers and the app clipboard hold the unmasked value
   (src/sase/ace/tui/widgets/secret_vim_text_area.py:1-24), and ACE's clipboard
   delivery emits OSC 52, which escapes to tmux and the system clipboard.
4. Mobile gateway parity gap (reported by researcher B, not independently
   re-verified): the gateway accepts gate `option_inputs` with no
   Telegram-style secret refusal (sase-core crates/sase_gateway/src/routes.rs
   ~3040-3083), while sase-telegram refuses secret inputs.

Suggested remediation (from the consolidated research report): redact secret
fields from every sidecar and return payload (hand values to detached procs
via an inherited pipe/fd if truly needed); exclude secret fields from
value_digest (require re-entry on retry); add copy-out protection for secret
widgets (block yank/registers/OSC 52; keep paste-in so password managers
work); make the mobile gateway refuse secret-bearing gate actions, mirroring
Telegram. Item 4 crosses the Rust core boundary (sase-core gateway).

Full trace: research repo 202609/agent_sudo_requests/agent_sudo_requests__b.md
sections 3.3 and 5.5-5.6, and the consolidated report's section 6.

task_type_fields.impact: Any credential submitted through a secret: true gate input lands in plaintext proc sidecars and logs, leaves a dictionary-crackable digest in the gate journal, and can escape via vim registers/OSC 52 clipboard. Blocks safely using gate secret inputs for real credentials; prerequisite (Phase 0) for the planned agent sudo-request feature.
task_type_fields.repro: Read cli_answer.py:268-328 (option_inputs copied raw into the detached proc payload and echoed in the return dict), journal.py:74-76 (unsalted sha256 value_digest), and the SecretVimTextArea module docstring. Answer any shell-backed gate that declares a secret: true input, then inspect ~/.sase/procs/runtime/<proc>/operation-request.json for the plaintext value.
